task.description: Implement D1-D4 from the ISS-0170 diagnosis: a diagnostic CI pre-flight that distinguishes a GitHub Actions platform outage from a real failure, without introducing any mechanism capable of masking a genuine failure.
acceptance_criteria: Pre-flight step queries githubstatus.com components API for the Actions component
Outage surfaced as an explicit annotation naming the incident
Pre-check is diagnostic only: never fails the build, never masks a genuine failure
CLAUDE.md requires checking the status API before reporting red CI as acceptable

result.summary: All four ISS-0170 acceptance criteria satisfied and verified by execution. (1) tools/check_github_status.py queries https://www.githubstatus.com/api/v2/components.json for the ungrouped 'Actions' component; verified against the live API, which returned status=operational, degraded=false, exit 0, and independently confirmed by fetching the raw payload. (2) The ::warning:: annotation now names the incident AND its start time, impact and shortlink; a new --summary mode writes a durable Markdown section to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY. Both proven by injecting a synthetic major_outage payload shaped like the real 2026-08-06 incident. (3) Diagnostic only: main() returns 0 unconditionally, fetch() swallows all network/parse errors, and the degraded path was confirmed to exit 0. A programmatic audit of every step in ci.yml confirms no build, test or lint step carries continue-on-error or '|| true' as a result of this change. (4) CLAUDE.md's 'Never Call a Red Pipeline OK Without a Source' now states the status-API query as mandatory, adds a fourth outcome row for the unchecked case, and states explicitly that an open incident never converts a genuine failure into an acceptable one. The diagnostic was added to the build job (not only the sibling platform_status job) because during webhook-throttling outages that sibling job is itself liable to be cancelled. zig build exits 0; ci.yml parses under yaml.safe_load; lint_agent_docs.py reports 0 findings.
